items.claim: The onset argument turns on a class shift out of the statute that ends at MT 46:18 and into the guided circuit that the transport verb opens at MT 46:19, but only the onset side is carried in the row's evidence: MT 46:18 is argued in prose and mirrored by no reference of its own, so the close side of this seam rests on a class label rather than on the verse.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 46:19 opens with a transport verb, and the span holds two parallel panels, each closing on the guide's own speech - the priests' boiling places at 46:19-46:20 and the people's corner courts at 46:21-46:24 - the speech frame standing in 4 verses of this span (MT 46:20, 46:24, 47:6, 47:8, sweep over the span's 64 verses). Close side of the seam behind the row: MT 46:18 ends the prince's-inheritance statute, and nothing in the row's references carries it. The mark evidence favours the row rather than the alternative: the one mark inside the span follows MT 46:19 and therefore falls between the transport verb and the speech that explains it, inside the first panel, so it cannot mark a unit edge; the row discloses it as tier-3 single-witness evidence that does not cut. Judged from both sides the span stands at 46:19-46:24.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 46:18 is the last verse of the prince's-inheritance statute and is the close side of this row's onset seam; carry it as a reference of its own so the class shift is evidenced on both sides and not only on the onset

items.claim: The row's rejected alternative is the weaker of the two available: it weighs a split at MT 47:5/47:6 only as a way of isolating the measured wadings at 47:3-47:5, and says of them that no device bounds them, while MT 47:6 itself carries three onset-grade devices at once - the speech frame, the son-of-man address, and two transport verbs - which are the very devices that cut a seam inside a vision; the alternative that was never weighed is the one the text marks.
items.both_sides: Onset side of the unweighed alternative: MT 47:6 carries the speech frame, the son-of-man address that the address inventory lists at this verse, and two transport verbs, and a seam inside a vision is ruled to sit on a transport or speech verse. Close side: MT 47:5 carries no close device at all - the measuring simply stops - and the speech frame recurs at MT 47:8 inside the explanation that follows, so cutting at every speech verse would over-split the river vision. That absent close on the left of 47:6, not the absence of a bounding device around 47:3-47:5, is what keeps 47:1-47:12 one unit, and it is what the row should have said: the span is right and the reason given for it is not the strongest one. The span's own outer seams are sound: a transport verb opens 47:1, and the mark inventory records a setumah after MT 47:12 with the messenger formula opening a new genre at 47:13. Weighing the 12-verse length matters here too, since the ruled target is 7 to 10 verses and the wider allowance is given to the measured and listed blocks of chs 40-42, 45 and 48, not to ch 47.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 47:6 carries the speech frame, the son-of-man address and two transport verbs, and is therefore the strongest alternative seam inside this vision; it is rejected because MT 47:5 carries no close device and the speech frame recurs at MT 47:8 inside the same explanation

items.claim: The close warrant at MT 48:7 does not distinguish that verse from the six before it and the seam behind 48:8 is straddled: the one-portion phrase ends all 7 verses of MT 48:1-48:7, so it cannot mark where the block stops, and 12 verses of ch 48 open with the same frame, MT 48:8 among them, its 8 opening consonantal-skeleton tokens repeating 7 of MT 48:7's with only the name slot changed - and that name is the one that ends MT 48:7. The row discloses none of this continuity against its own closing seam.
items.both_sides: Close side: MT 48:7 ends with the same one-portion phrase that ends MT 48:1 through 48:6 (7 of 7 verses), and the mark inventory records nothing after MT 48:7, so neither a device nor a mark marks an end there. Onset side: MT 48:8 opens with the frame the portion verses use - 12 verses of ch 48 open with it - and only its second half turns to the offering, whose sanctuary-in-the-middle clause is what actually changes the listed object. So the seam rests on that change of object alone, which can stand; what is missing is the mandatory disclosure that a byte-true frame runs across it, carrying the preceding portion's own name into the onset verse. The row's other seam is sound: the list heading opens MT 48:1 and the ruled architecture treats that heading as a cutting onset, and the refrain block is left uncut.

suggested_fix.fact: the one-portion phrase ends all 7 verses of MT 48:1-48:7 and so does not mark the block's end, and the opening frame of MT 48:7 recurs at the head of MT 48:8 on the consonantal skeleton with the name slot carrying Judah, the portion named at the end of MT 48:7; disclose both as continuity evidence against the 48:7/48:8 seam

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Paseq disclosure is asymmetric across this cluster and I cannot resolve whether the omission is a defect. The paseq inventory lists occurrences inside two rows that disclose none - MT 47:9 and MT 47:12 twice in the row spanning 47:1-47:12, and MT 47:16 and MT 47:17 in the row spanning 47:13-47:23 - while the four rows in ch 48 disclose the occurrences in their spans (MT 48:1, 48:7, 48:22, 48:35).
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: the K/Q rule is explicit that a row covering a site discloses it, which is why I called the ch-48 omission a defect; the paseq rule is written as count-only with no per-row disclosure duty, so calling the ch-47 omission a defect would mean inventing a rule. The asymmetry is measured and real and belongs to the controlling agent, not to me.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The transport-verb sweep's membership at MT 46:21. The sweep of 20 verses does not include 46:21, yet 46:21 opens with a transport verb of the same family and carries a second one, as the row itself discloses; measured over this cluster's span the transport forms fall at MT 46:19, 46:21, 47:1, 47:2 and 47:6, which is one verse more than the sweep names here.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: if the sweep is meant to catch that form its membership is one verse short, which is the same class of discrepancy as the dateline count that was reported upward rather than patched. It is not a defect in the row, which reports the bytes honestly; it is a question about the sweep.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the low-severity findings on the two mark-absence rows should instead be recorded as passes. Both absence statements are measured true, and my challenge is against their form - a denial carried inside a comma chain, and an impossibility asserted where only an absence is measurable.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: the rewording rule handed to me treats a denial behind a comma as a rewording order rather than a pass, and the suite flagged both rows independently, so I recorded them as low challenges rather than softening them; if that rule is read more narrowly, these two become supports and the counts move to 3 supports and 4 challenges.
